name: Brick rose
lede: Brick rose is a dusty, reddish pink documented only in Ridgway's 1912 standards and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, and rare in our painting archive.

sections.title: A quiet modifier on rose
sections.body: Our library carries Brick rose from Ridgway's 1912 standards and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which classes a close match as a grayish red [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[copper-rose]], [[marsh-rose]], [[hydrangea-red]] and [[swiss-rose]], at 3, 3.6, 3.9 and 4.5 ΔE [1]. In printed English the two-word phrase rose fastest in the 1850s and peaked in use in the 1920s, by our Ngram data, though that count mixes every sense of the words, including actual bricks and roses [2]. Our library lists no everyday near-duplicate for this swatch[1]. It sits in, [[dusty-rose]] and [[rosewood]], all darker, grayer cousins of plain [[rose]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Brick rose in only 109 of 23,781 paintings (0.46 percent), as photographed[2]. It is over-represented in paintings from India (2.6 times expected) and in the Kalighat school especially, at 6.9 times its baseline [2]. It most often plays an accent inside a painting [2]. The earliest dated match, from 1000, is nine centuries before the 1912 record, a gap the archive's thin early coverage explains rather than the color's true age, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
